slides.texte_overlay:
habits that make you
fearless in any room

speaking first

say something in the first five minutes of any meeting or class. the longer you wait, the harder it gets, so speaking early takes the pressure off completely.

holding eye contact

hold someone's gaze for one extra second when you greet them. it feels small, but it tells everyone in the room that you're completely comfortable being seen.

always having a story

spend 5 minutes a day learning something surprising, and you'll never be stuck for words again. having a story ready takes away most of the fear of walking into a room.
slides.texte_sophia:
always having a story

i used to go silent in new rooms. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a strange myth or a planet, and i always have a story ready to share.

slides.texte_overlay:
walking in slowly

walk into rooms a little slower than feels natural. a calm entrance makes you look settled and sure, and your body slowly convinces your mind to follow.

asking good questions

ask people about the things they love. curious questions take the attention off your nerves and make you the person everyone quietly enjoys talking to.
